chunks: And it has been narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A tree, its root is in the non-sacred area and its branch is in the Haram. So he said: “Its root is forbidden because of the place of its branch.”
I said: Then if its root is in the Haram and its branch is in the non-sacred area? He said: “Its branch is forbidden because of the place of its root.”

key_terms.أَصْلُهَا: its root or base location, which affects the ruling
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary area with special legal protections
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: the non-sacred area outside the Haram boundary
key_terms.حُرِّمَ: it was made forbidden or protected from violation in this context
key_terms.شَجَرَةٌ: a tree under discussion in the legal ruling
key_terms.فَرْعُهَا: its branch, whose location is legally considered
key_terms.لِمَكَانِ: because of the location or place

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a tree whose roots or branches extend between the Haram and the non-sacred area?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a tree connected to the Haram and the non-sacred area. It establishes that the ruling follows the part connected to the Haram, so what lies outside may take the sanctity-based prohibition of what lies inside.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2341 - It has been narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a tree whose root is in the non-sacred area (hill) and its branches extend into the sacred area (Haram).
Imam (as) replied: "The root is sanctified because of the branch's location."

I then asked: "What if its root is in the Haram and its branch extends into the hill?"
Imam (as) said: "The branch is sanctified because of the root's location."
